newsitem.title: USA: Lear sets wireless phone pact.
newsitem.headline: Lear sets wireless phone pact.

text.p: Automotive interior supplier Lear Corp said Thursday it completed a licensing agreement with CellPort Labs Inc to produce embedded car kits for portable, wireless telephones.
The kits would allow hands-free operation of wireless, also called cellular, telephones.
The devices would also power any model of portable phone, charge the phone's battery and provide an external antenna that boosts range and clarity.

Lear spokeswoman Leslie Touma said the company will begin immediately talking with automakers about purchasing the kits. She said the deal is the first of its kind and would offer a device Lear's competitors do not currently have.
"We think it's a great consumer convenience and safety item," said Touma.

Based in Boulder, Colorado, CellPort specializes in universal wireless connectivity technology. The firm said its patented Universal Car Kit allows consumers to use any cellular, or other wireless terminal in their vehicles, and is compatible with all wireless communications network protocols.

CellPort President Pat Kennedy said there are 43 million cellular telephone subscribers in the U.S. About 85 percent of all U.S. wireless phone sales are for portable, or hand-held units, versus those connected to vehicles, he said.

Globally, there are an estimated 140 million wireless subscribers, with more than 90 percent of sales being hand- held units, said Kennedy. Several countries, including England, Italy, Brazil and Australia require telephones used in cars to be hands-free. The U.S. does not.
Lear is one of the world's largest vehicle interior suppliers, with 1995 sales of $4.7 billion.
